title: Monthly Research Reports 39.
subject: Monthly Research Reports 39.
section: To study the pretreatment of tobacco and its effect on the polycyclic hydrocarbon content of the smoke condensate.
procedures: Solvent extraction of tobacco prior to fabrication into cigarettes to remove the precursor(s) from the tobacco of the polycyclic hydrocarbons in the smoke.
Use of more effective and selective filtering agents (see Expt. No. 19, Table I).
Addition of compounds to the tobacco to alter both the rate and temperature of combustion.
findings: Polycyclic hydrocarbon content and/or the carcinogenic activity of cigarette smoke can be reduced by one of the following procedures.

Consideration of the possible precursors of the polycyclic hydrocarbons in the smoke led to the inclusion of the terpenoid compounds and the sterols together with the aliphatic saturated hydrocarbons.

Recent chemical and biological evidence from other laboratories have indicated that the main precursors may be either the terpenoid compounds, e.g., solanesol, or the sterols, e.g., stigmasterol and β-sitosterol, or both, with the aliphatic saturated hydrocarbons occupying a lesser role as polycyclic hydrocarbon precursors.
